Where it began

Emilio Gay was born in Bedford on 14 April 2000 and went to school there, at Bedford School. His family background stretches well beyond the town: his father's side came from Grenada, and his mother is part Italian, which turned out to matter for his cricket later on.

He joined the Northamptonshire academy at under-15 level and was named its Player of the Year in 2018. A first professional contract followed in 2019, and his first-class debut came that September against Gloucestershire. The weather had other ideas, though, and he had to wait until the following season to bat in it.

The player

He made his first first-class hundred in June 2021, 101 against Kent at Canterbury. The big one came in April 2024: 261 against Middlesex, from 401 balls, the highest score by a Northamptonshire batter in a Championship match between the two counties. Later that summer he agreed a three-year move to Durham.

In 2025 he played Twenty20 internationals for Italy, opening the batting and making a half-century against Scotland in only his second match. A strong start to the 2026 county season then brought an England Test call. He made his debut against New Zealand on 4 June 2026, scoring eight and then 57 in the second innings. On 9 September 2026 he made his third Test fifty, against Pakistan. By November 2026 he had played 6 Tests, scoring 271 runs at 24.64, with three fifties and a best of 60, and holding 8 catches.

What made him special

Patience is the word for his best innings. Facing 401 balls for a double hundred takes a cool head as well as a sound method, and in his first six Tests he got past fifty three times.

A Test hundred had not yet arrived by November 2026, but for a man who once waited a whole winter to start his first innings, waiting has never seemed to trouble him much.

Away from the middle

He has spent time on the other side of the microphone too, joining the BBC commentary team for The Hundred in 2026. He was also picked for England Lions in 2025, to face India A, before the full Test call came.

And finally

Not many cricketers can say they played international cricket for one country and Test cricket for another within a year. Fewer can say the weather made them wait until the next season to bat in their first-class debut.
